clue.text: Move on board but keep location

definitions.meaning: in chess, castling is a move made on the board with king and rook
a keep is the central tower of a fortress

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift position while somehow staying put, like a puzzling order to a removal firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess manoeuvre swapping king and rook, and a castle is the fortress that houses a keep.

clue.text: Think vital part of system maybe wore away

parts.note: a cog is a small but vital part of a machine
IT, information technology, is one kind of system
ate away means wore away, eroded

explanation.surface: Pondering how some vital part of a system may have worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to ponder or reflect, a formal word for think.

clue.text: Seen leaving Easter Sunday assembly the day before

indicators.note: these letters depart from the longer phrase
the remaining letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spotted slipping away from an Easter Sunday gathering the previous day.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, E, E, N out of EASTER SUNDAY ('leaving') and rearrange the rest ('assembly').
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday falls immediately before Sunday, in this case Holy Saturday before Easter.

clue.text: Othello incensed part is cut

indicators.note: a part of the words holds the answer

explanation.surface: Part of Othello is cut because it inflamed audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: othelLO INcensed holds the answer; 'cut' is a butcher's cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a joint of meat taken from either side of the backbone, a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Content to design it in green kindling

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what sits inside it, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A gardener happy to plan a design in green while laying a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy', but it means what is contained: desIGN IT IN Green.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling, as a verb form, means setting light to something, the same sense as igniting.

clue.text: Abandoned economic control of benchmark

definitions.meaning: the monetary system tying currency to gold, abandoned by Britain in 1931
the best example against which others are measured

explanation.surface: A defunct economic policy described as the benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the old gold-pegged currency system and, figuratively, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Press club's tough element

definitions.meaning: to ... clothes is to press them
... as an adjective means hard, as in an ... will

explanation.surface: A press club with a hard core.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers smoothing clothes, a golf club, firmness of will, and metal number 26 on the periodic table.

clue.text: No use organising seditious fools

indicators.note: saying no to these letters means taking them away
the remaining letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fools plotting sedition get nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U, S, E out of SEDITIOUS ('No') and rearrange the rest ('organising').
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are stupid people, the same as fools.

clue.text: Finally Daniel Craig arranged protection from 19

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order
only the end letter of the name is used

explanation.surface: Daniel Craig, as Bond, finally set up a shield against the undead.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is VAMPIRES; 'Finally' gives L, and 'arranged' shuffles L and CRAIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore holds that this pungent bulb wards off vampires, the answer to 19.

clue.text: Turn largely intimate in dark

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: close friends are thick, as in 'thick as thieves'

explanation.surface: A moment of turning close and intimate in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of THICK, leaving THIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic style evokes gloom and the macabre, so it can stand for dark in mood.

clue.text: John dead in coffin is comparatively gory

indicators.note: placed in the coffin means set inside the word for it

parts.note: a bier carries a coffin, so the setter treats them as one
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a man called John lying dead in his coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is a toilet, not a man. A bier is strictly the stand a coffin rests on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodier is the comparative of bloody, meaning more gory, so 'is comparatively gory' describes it.

clue.text: Producers of sound novels I'll coo about

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cooing over novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Violoncellos, cellos in full, are string instruments, and instruments produce sound.

clue.text: See 27
See 16
Hear a quaint case

indicators.note: asks the solver to listen to how the phrase is spoken

parts.note: quaint means twee, so the phrase gives 'a twee'

explanation.surface: Listening to an old-fashioned lawsuit, a quaint case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a twee' said aloud matches the word for the small case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and similar items.

clue.text: Alphabet soup chosen over tasty first course

indicators.note: the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Alphabet soup picked ahead of something tasty to start a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first course' looks like a starter; 'first' is the signal and 'course' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Completion of cycle without first gear damaged fingernails

indicators.note: the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
this letter is left out of the word
only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Finishing a cycle without first gear and hurting your nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives G, 'without' takes it from FINGERNAILS, and 'damaged' shuffles the remainder. 'cycle' is a washing machine's, not a bicycle's.
explanation.definitionFit: The final rinse is the last stage of a washing machine's programme.

clue.text: Naval in-trays organised by region

indicators.note: sorting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A navy's office trays sorted region by region.
explanation.definitionFit: Transylvania is a historical area of Romania, home of the Dracula legend.

clue.text: Material relative is after dollars

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: bucks is slang for dollars
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A relative chasing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckskin is soft leather made from deer hide, a material for clothing.

clue.text: Measure of current powers held by extortionists

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: vires is Latin for powers, as in ultra vires
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Electrical powers seized by blackmailers.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire figuratively is a person who preys on others, bleeding them of money.

clue.text: Number with credit maybe returning mid-July with a villain

parts.note: to count is a number, a tally

indicators.note: coming back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a credit card is one sort of card

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A tally of credit returned in mid-July, bound up with some villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CARD into DRAC; 'mid-' takes UL from July.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula is the vampire antagonist of Stoker's novel, a classic literary villain.

clue.text: Fell over Coniston pensioner

definitions.meaning: the ... of Coniston is a fell, a hill in the Lake District, above the village of Coniston

explanation.surface: A pensioner who tumbled over at Coniston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' is a hill, not a tumble. Gary Oldman also played Dracula in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner is someone elderly, and the Lake District peak shares the name.

clue.text: Actor of 20 luckily got silent parts

indicators.note: the first two letters of each word

explanation.surface: An actor who luckily landed silent film roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is COUNT DRACULA; 'parts' takes the opening pair of letters from luckily, got and silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Lugosi played the vampire in the 1931 film, the role he is famous for.

clue.text: Praise God in speech

indicators.note: spoken, the word matches another of the same sound

parts.note: the Lord is God

explanation.surface: Worshippers praising God in what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to extol or glorify, a straight synonym of praise as a verb.

clue.text: Core problem for the R & A

indicators.note: a problem makes a mess of things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fundamental difficulty facing the R & A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews.
explanation.walkthrough: The R & A is golf's governing body, based at St Andrews in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or core.

clue.text: Don't bother with small sleep

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
kip is British slang for a sleep or nap

explanation.surface: Advice not to bother with a brief nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to omit it or not bother doing it.

clue.text: Asian flower scattered throughout Kuwait

indicators.note: the answer's letters are dotted through the name, with the extra letters dropped

explanation.surface: A flower of Asia found growing all over Kuwait.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Kwai of Thailand. Drop U and T from KUWAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kwai is a river in Thailand, made famous by the bridge film; a river flows.

clue.text: Headline act could begin to jar

parts.note: to begin is to start
an urn is a jar or vase

explanation.surface: A headliner who could make a jar start.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main attraction of a show, the headline performer.

clue.text: Dance move with small steps for man

definitions.text: Dance move with small steps for man

parts.words: Dance move with small steps for man
parts.note: a gliding backward dance move that also recalls Neil Armstrong's 'one small step for man' on the lunar surface

explanation.surface: A dance in which a man takes small steps.
explanation.walkthrough: It is both Michael Jackson's backward-gliding move and Armstrong's 1969 stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a famous dance step and also the first astronaut excursion on the lunar surface.

clue.text: Fireman sent first to king and queen

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A firefighter dispatched first to attend royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A fireman in the old sense tends a furnace, as on a steam train; Bram Stoker wrote Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker feeds coal to a furnace or boiler, the older sense of fireman on locomotives and ships.

clue.text: Most loud and upset signatories lose rag

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Angry signatories at their most vocal, losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SIGNATORIES once R, A, G are taken away; 'lose' marks those letters as going. 'lose rag' surface-reads as losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisiest is the superlative of noisy, so it means loudest.

clue.text: Medic signs for a round

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
to ink a deal is to sign it

explanation.surface: A doctor signing off on a round of visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying a round means buying drinks for a whole group in a pub.
